opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kenneth Burch (employee ID E007) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E007.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kenneth Burch (E007) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; the Analyst role does not own Payroll, so admin is not permitted. Write is within policy, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kenneth Burch (E007) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; admin never. Requested write exceeds the maximum for a contractor with basic training, so recommend granting read.
reason: I relied on the HR record for employment type, which is HR's domain: Kenneth Burch (E007) is a full-time Analyst. As a full-time employee, the maximum access is write; admin is not permitted because the Analyst role does not own Payroll (owned by Payroll Specialist). The requested level (write) is at or below this maximum, so I grant write. (Note: the Security agent's record conflicts on employment type, but employment type is an HR fact.)
